Austin (eds.), Language Documentation and Description 11: 136-230. London: SOAS. doi:10.25894/LDD181 (electronic version July 2014; landinghttps://www.lddjournal.org/article/id/1150/).
tone_statements.quote: It has occasionally been claimed that lexical tone exists in some of the Northern Aslian languages (Schebesta 1928b: 205; Phaiboon 1984; Bishop 1996a). ... The majority of Mon-Khmer languages, including the majority of Aslian languages, lack lexical tone. It occurs in Vietnamese and some other Mon-Khmer languages, where it is known to be a secondary development (Haudricourt 1954). Hajek (2003) carefully analysed the claims for lexical tone in Northern Aslian and concluded that some of the languages may exhibit lexical tone, but that it carries a low functional load and is expressed differently by different speakers.
tone_statements.summary: Aslian generally: no lexical tone (claims only for N. Aslian Kensiw/Jahai; register only in Mah Meri); Semaq Beri: nothing reported.

sources.note: Section 4.2.2 'Tone and register' (pp. 185-186): lexical tone has been claimed only for some Northern Aslian languages (Schebesta 1928b, Phaiboon 1984, Bishop 1996a; Kensiw guj 'head' high vs g@j 'language' mid), 'the majority of Aslian languages lack lexical tone'; Hajek 2003 finds low-functional-load tone in N. Aslian; Wnuk 2010 and Burenhult 2005 deny tone for Maniq and Jahai; phonation register known only in Mah Meri (an innovation). Nothing tonal is reported for Semaq Beri or any Southern Aslian language other than Mah Meri register.

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2003. Aslian: Mon-Khmer of the Malay Peninsula. Mon-Khmer Studies 33: 1-58.

tone.quote: [p. 16:] Contrastive length has been lost by the whole Northern Aslian group, as well as by Semoq Beri (Southern). ... [p. 16 fn.:] Perhaps this is because Aslian did not develop register distinctions, which can be demonstrated to have promoted the rampant diphthongization in such languages as Mon and Khmer. ... [p. 18:] The final laryngeals /-h, -ʔ/, another general Mon-Khmer feature, are well preserved in Aslian, so there is no question of their engendering tonal or registral effects on the previous vowel, as in Vietnamese.
tone.locator: pp. 16 and 18, section 1.1 (c) Vowels and (d) Final consonants
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: Aslian: no register, no tonogenetic effects from final laryngeals (family-level); Semaq Beri: vowel length contrast lost.
